note:
v1, THE SKELETON of the third song, "PLAIN HUNT" (Harry: "answered clips. unlock a third track slot!"). The whole shape is standing, bare; no voice yet.
THE IDEA: a third kind of long cycle. English church bells cannot play tunes; ringers ring CHANGES: the bells strike once each, in a row, and from one row to the next a bell may only swap places with its neighbour, by a rule that visits every possible order exactly once and comes back to where it began. Here the riff is that row: six sixteenths, five notes that change places (Eb C B Ab Gb, the album's hook notes running down) and a low F that always comes last. It is rung through two whole cycles, 240 rows, no two alike within either, and each ends on the scale it began on. The highest note walks later and later through the riff and back, all piece long; the kick goes with it and a church bell doubles it.
THE SHAPE (5:05): 0:00 church bells alone ring the scale down, slowly. 0:10 the band takes it up at twice the speed. 0:25 the order starts to change: the first cycle, on F, then up to A flat (1:02), then B (1:40), the drums harder each time. 2:17 it has come round: one chord, and the bells alone again. 2:37 the second cycle, by a different rule, on F, A flat (3:15) and C (3:52). 4:30 the landing: the scale again on F, with the bells ringing it over the band at half speed. 4:52 one chord, and the lowest bell tolls three times.

Does the riff sound like a riff that keeps mutating, or like a scale exercise? Can you hear the accent (the high note, the kick, the bell) sliding through it? Church bells on a metal record: ominous, or cheesy?
WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): compscore 100.00 / 100.00 (seeds 0 and 11); the scorer finds the cycle of six against the bar. File -10.0 LUFS, true peak -1.29, no flat-topping.
- The generator rings both methods and checks each: 120 rows, all different, the last one the scale.
- It is double-tracked from the start: two takes a side through two amps (your "double track em" on Common Time's landing, taken here too). The snare has the room you asked for.
- On the groove it sits where the other two sit: full sections -16.3 to -16.8 LUFS raw; the bells alone -21.2 and -20.1.
- The bells: 11 dB under the mix where one doubles the high note, 8 dB under in the landing.
WHAT IS BARE: one rig throughout; nothing but the kit changes between the two cycles; the middle is only bells, a drone and a pad; no lead, no voice.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether five notes changing places at this speed read as a riff; whether the accent's walk is heard.
NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

note:
v2, THE TOWER GETS ITS VOICES AND A GONG (palette round: instruments swapped for ones no other track on the album has). Where the bells ring alone (the opening, the middle at 2:17, the end) they rang over a bowed bass drone and a synth pad, the same two all three songs used. Both have left this song. Under the bells there is now a CHANT: two low men's voices a fifth apart, the mouth moving slowly between "o" and "u", with a bowed horsehair drone on the low F as their floor. And a GONG is struck twice: when the first cycle comes round (2:17) and on the last chord (4:52).
It is also a first answer to "the voice needs work": this is a different voice from the one that speaks in the other two songs (a different way of making one). If it sounds like men singing to you, it is a voice I can use there.

Men chanting, or a synth pad? Does the gong make the moment it comes round, or is it one thing too many?
WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): compscore 100.00 / 100.00 (seeds 0 and 11), as v1: kept on judgment. File -10.0 LUFS, true peak -1.29, no flat-topping.
- Nothing in the heavy sections changed.
- Under the bells the chant sits 7 dB below them and its floor 2 to 3 dB below the chant; the bells still lead.
- The chant voice is all mouth and no chest: nearly everything it has is between 250 and 500 Hz. That is why it has a floor under it. Without one the song lost its low end in those passages (the scorer noticed: 99.82).
- On the groove the bells-alone passages are about 1 dB louder (-20.1 and -19.5 LUFS raw); the gong makes the bar it is struck in 0.8 to 1.1 dB louder.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the chant reads as voices; whether the bowed drone under it is a floor or a buzz.
NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.
